newsitem.title: UK: S&P rates Spinnaker corp credit B plus.
newsitem.headline: S&P rates Spinnaker corp credit B plus.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Wednesday it assigned its B plus corporate credit rating to Spinnaker Industries Inc.
Additionally, S&P said it assigned its B rating to the company's $100 million senior secured notes due 2006 (Rule 144A).
The outlook is stable, S&P said.
"Initial ratings on Dallas-based Spinnaker Industries reflect a below- average business position, thin cash flow coverages, and aggressive financial management," S&P said.
The company also has a limited operating history, as its business mix consists primarily of two adhesive-backed materials operations acquired in the past two years, S&P said.

The October 1995 acquisition of Central Products for about $80 million made Spinnaker a leading U.S. manufacturer in adhesive carton sealing tapes, while the September 1994 purchase of Brown Bridge for about $30 million provided a decent market position in adhesive-backed label stock, S&P said.

Although the firm benefits from some strong market shares in niche markets and economies of scale, competition is intense, stemming from some much larger rivals and substitute products. Growth rates appear to be strong, about two times GDP, driven by increased labeling regulations and convenience over alternative products, S&P said.

While some of the products manufactured by the firm have commodity characteristics, cost reduction initiatives and capacity expansion programs should improve earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) margins to 10 percent over the next few years, S&P said.

Spinnaker is expected to increase debt usage in order to fund potential "bolt-on" acquisitions, elevating financial risk. Thus, EBITDA interest coverage should average near 2.0 times and funds from operations to debt should average 10 percent.
Financial flexibility is constrained, although a light maturity schedule and access to equity markets could aid liquidity, S&P said.

"Although potential acquisitions are expected to keep debt at aggressive levels, earnings and cash flow protection should gradually improve due to profitability enhancements and solid market growth prospects, S&P said.
